guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 1
guides.title: Water, Acids, Bases and Buffers
guides.lede: Where the body’s water is, how water and salts move between compartments, what pH means, and how buffers, lungs and kidneys keep blood pH between 7.35 and 7.45.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 2
guides.title: Structures of the Major Compounds of the Body
guides.lede: The building blocks of every later lecture: carbon skeletons and functional groups, then carbohydrates, lipids and the nitrogen-containing compounds.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 3
guides.title: Amino Acids in Proteins
guides.lede: The 20 (plus one) building blocks of proteins: their structure, how they are grouped, what special jobs some of them do, how proteins are modified after they are made, and how protein sequences vary.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 4
guides.title: Structure–Function Relationships in Proteins
guides.lede: The four levels of protein structure, what holds each one together, how proteins fold, unfold and get destroyed, and the diseases of misfolding: Alzheimer disease and Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 5
guides.title: Phospholipids, Sphingolipids and Eicosanoids
guides.lede: The membrane lipids built on glycerol and on sphingosine, what they do in signalling, the lung, the mitochondrion and the nerve, the storage diseases when their breakdown fails, and the eicosanoids that drive inflammation and clotting.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 6
guides.title: The Extracellular Matrix and Fibrous Proteins
guides.lede: What fills the space between cells: collagen, elastin, laminin, proteoglycans, integrins, fibronectin and the enzymes that remodel them, plus the diseases when any of these go wrong.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 7
guides.title: Globular Proteins: Hemoglobin and Myoglobin
guides.lede: How heme proteins bind oxygen, why hemoglobin’s curve is S-shaped and myoglobin’s is not, what shifts the curve, and the hemoglobin diseases: thalassemias, sickle cell, HbC, methemoglobinemia and CO poisoning.
topics: Biochem Wk 7: Globular Proteins (Hb and Mb)

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 1
guides.title: Introduction to Genetics and Mendel’s First Postulates
guides.lede: The words every later lecture uses (gene, allele, locus, genotype, phenotype…), the human genome in numbers, Mendel’s first three postulates, the sources and types of genetic variation, and sickle-cell anemia as the classic link from DNA to disease.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 2
guides.title: Incomplete Dominance, Codominance and the ABO System
guides.lede: When alleles don’t follow simple dominance: intermediate heterozygotes (pink flowers, Tay–Sachs carriers), both alleles expressed side by side (MN and ABO blood groups), and how a second gene can hide ABO completely (the Bombay phenotype).

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 3
guides.title: Gene Interaction, X-Linkage, Penetrance and Imprinting
guides.lede: How two genes shape one trait (epistasis and its modified ratios), how one gene shapes many traits (pleiotropy), X-linked and sex-dependent inheritance, why the same genotype can look different (penetrance, expressivity), and parent-of-origin effects (Prader–Willi and Angelman).

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 4
guides.title: Chromosome Mapping and Linkage
guides.lede: How geneticists find where genes sit on a chromosome without looking at it: crossing over, map units, the three-point test cross, DNA markers and genome databases, plus sister chromatid exchange and Bloom syndrome.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 5
guides.title: Sex Determination and Differentiation in Humans
guides.lede: How the father’s sperm decides genetic sex, what the X and Y chromosomes carry, how SRY switches on the testis pathway, how hormones then build male or female anatomy, the Y genes needed for sperm (AZF), and the three human sex ratios.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 6
guides.title: Dosage Compensation, X-Inactivation and Barr Bodies
guides.lede: Why females switch off one X chromosome in every cell, how to count Barr bodies, why some genes escape and still matter in Turner and Klinefelter syndromes, the Lyon hypothesis and mosaicism, and the molecular switch (XIST, TSIX, XITE).

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Week 7
guides.title: Nondisjunction and Sex Chromosome Aneuploidies
guides.lede: What goes wrong when chromosomes fail to separate in meiosis, and the four main results for the sex chromosomes: Klinefelter (47,XXY), Turner (45,X), triple X (47,XXX) and 47,XYY, plus how FISH confirms them.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 1
guides.title: Basic Properties of Cells: Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes
guides.lede: How cells were discovered, the cell theory, how big cells and their parts are, the basic properties every cell shares, and the fundamental split between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
topics: MB Lec 1: Cells, Prokaryote vs Eukaryote

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 2
guides.title: Types of Cells, Viruses, Viroids and Model Organisms
guides.lede: The two prokaryotic domains (Archaea, Bacteria), the kinds of eukaryotic cells and how they specialise, what viruses are and how they replicate (lytic and lysogenic), viroids, and the six model organisms of research.
topics: MB Lec 2: Cell Types, Viruses & Model Organisms

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 3
guides.title: The Chemical Basis of Life: Macromolecules
guides.lede: The four kinds of organic molecules in a cell, functional groups, and the four macromolecules (carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, proteins), with a close look at DNA architecture, base pairing, DNA vs RNA, ribozymes and ATP.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 4
guides.title: Proteins: Structure, Folding and Misfolding
guides.lede: Amino acids and peptide bonds, the four levels of protein structure (with myoglobin, domains and hemoglobin as examples), Anfinsen’s self-assembly experiment, chaperones and chaperonins, and diseases of protein structure.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Mitochondria
guides.title: Mitochondria and Cellular Respiration
guides.lede: Why oxygen changed life, the structure of the mitochondrion (two membranes, cristae, matrix, its own DNA), the three stages of respiration, how the electron transport chain and ATP synthase make ATP, uncouplers and brown fat, and three mitochondrial diseases.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 7
guides.title: The Endomembrane System and Protein Sorting
guides.lede: The membrane organelles that work as one unit (ER, Golgi, lysosomes, endosomes, vacuoles), the biosynthetic, secretory and endocytic pathways, signal sequences, the jobs of rough and smooth ER, the Golgi, lysosomes and peroxisomes, and the diseases added for the midterm.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 1
guides.title: Histology and Its Methods of Study
guides.lede: What histology studies, how a piece of tissue becomes a stained slide (fixation to sectioning), how H&E staining works, and the special methods that find specific molecules: autoradiography, cell culture, enzyme histochemistry, immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridisation.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 2
guides.title: Microscopy
guides.lede: The five kinds of light microscope (bright-field, fluorescence, phase-contrast, confocal, polarizing), resolving power, the two electron microscopes (TEM and SEM), and how to interpret sections and their artifacts.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 3
guides.title: The Plasma Membrane, Transport and Signalling
guides.lede: Cell differentiation, the structure of the plasma membrane (lipids, proteins, glycocalyx, lipid rafts), how molecules cross it (diffusion, channels, carriers, pumps), endocytosis and exocytosis, and how cells receive signals.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 4
guides.title: Ribosomes, Endoplasmic Reticulum and Golgi Apparatus
guides.lede: The cytoplasm, ribosomes and polysomes, rough ER (signal sequence, SRP, ERAD), smooth ER (lipids, detoxification, calcium) and the Golgi apparatus (cis and trans faces, COP coats, processing).

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 5
guides.title: Lysosomes, Proteasomes and Peroxisomes
guides.lede: The cell’s three clean-up and detox systems: lysosomes (acid hydrolases, M6P, heterolysosomes, residual bodies, autophagy), proteasomes (ubiquitin, ATP) and peroxisomes (H 2 O 2 , catalase, β-oxidation). Mitochondria from the same deck are in the Lecture 6 guide.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 6
guides.title: Mitochondria and Cytoplasmic Inclusions
guides.lede: Mitochondrial structure and ATP synthesis, their role in apoptosis, how they divide and why they look like bacteria; then the inclusions you see in electron micrographs: glycogen granules, lipid droplets, pigments and secretory granules. Built from the mitochondria slides of the Lecture 5 deck and the “Organelles” image set.

guides.subject: gct
guides.label: Lecture 7
guides.title: The Cytoskeleton
guides.lede: The three protein filament systems of the cell: microtubules (tubulin, MTOC, kinesin and dynein), microfilaments (actin, treadmilling, cortex) and intermediate filaments (keratins, vimentin family, neurofilaments, lamins).
